                  <ns0:p n="47">47 Remember how short my time <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Our time, the time of our king and kingdom, in whose name the Psalmist puts up this petition, and about whom he was much more solicitous than about himself, as is evident both from the following verses and from the whole body of the Psalm. The sence seems to be this, Our king and all his people, and I among the rest, are short-lived and perishing creatures, that of themselves and according to the course of nature must shortly die. And therefore there is no need that thou shouldest add further afflictions to sweep them away before their time.</ns0:note> is: where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore hast thou made all men in vain! <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Wherefore hast thou made us and our King (and consequently all other men whose conditi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on is in nothing better than ours, and in respect of thy grace and mercy is much worse than ours) in vain or to so little purpose? Didst thou raise us and him, establish us for thy people, settle the crown upon <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> and his seed for ever by a solemn and unchangeable Covenant, erect a magnificent and glorious Temple, and vouchsafe so many and great promises and priviledges, and all this but for a few years, that our Crown and glory should be taken from us within a little time after it was put upon our heads, that our Kingdom should be broken almost as soon as it was firmly esta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />blished, that thy worship should be so soon corrupted, and thy Temple quickly robbed, and not long after fre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quently abused, and polluted and wasted, and now at last utterly demolished? It is not strange that such considerations as these did fill the Psalmists mind with amusement and sad and perplexing thoughts. Nor doth the Psalmist accuse or upbraid God herewith, but onely useth it as an argument to move God to repair and restore their decayed state, that they might live to praise and serve and glorify him, and not be such useless and insignificant Creatures as now they were in this forlorn estate of things, and as they should be if they should go into the place and state of the dead before the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stitution of their broken State and Kingdom.</ns0:note>

                  <ns0:p n="51">51 Wherewith thine enemies have reproach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, O LORD, wherewith they have reproach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed the footsteps of thine anointed <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>of thy Messiah.</ns0:hi> By whom he seems to understand ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther first the Kings of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> the singular number being put for the plural; and by their <ns0:hi>footsteps</ns0:hi> may be meant either their ways or actions, and the sad consequences thereof; or the traces or memorials of their antient splendor and domi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nion, wherewith they now upbraid them; Or rather second<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly the Messiah most properly and eminently so called; of whom not onely many Christians, but the Chaldee Paraphrast and the Hebrew Doctors, understand this place. And this suits very well both with the singular number here used which points at one particular and eminent person anointed by God to be the King of his People, and with the matter and occa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion of this Psalm. Poole.heading:
PSAL. LXXXIX. 
                     
                        Or, a psalm for Ethan the Ezrahite to give instruction. Maschil of 1 Chron. 2. 6. Ethan the Ezrahite Either first, He who is mentioned 1 Kings 4. 31. And then the Psalm is prophetical of things to come; which yet, after the manner of the Prophets, he represents as present. And this Prophetical Psalm might be left upon record as a cordial for Davids Family in their future distresses which Ethan by the spirit of Prophecy foresaw. Or secondly, some other person of the same name, and inspired by the same spirit, who had lived in the times of which the Psalmist here speaketh..
